# 3. KAIST

## A. University snapshot

| Field | Verified answer |

## Changes since 13 Sep 2026

- **Correction:** fee is now verified as **USD 80**, non-refundable. Kazakhstan is not within the published LDC waiver group.
- **Correction:** KAIST accepts **up to two optional recommendations**; it does not require one recommendation for Fall 2027.

- The Early application is open and closes **22 October 2026 at 18:00 KST**.
- Exact five 2027 written questions and limits are available.

## B. Programmes for this applicant

| Official programme | Degree / unit | Entry and prerequisites | Restrictions / change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Computer Science | Bachelor’s; School of Computing, College of Engineering | No direct-major entry. Strong mathematics/science preparation is encouraged; the admission guide does not set a CS-specific physics, calculus or programming minimum. | International applicants may select it in sophomore year without a quota or second admission stated on the admissions page. |
| AI Computing | Bachelor’s; School of AI, College of AI | Same undeclared entry; no programme-specific admission prerequisite published | Selectable in sophomore year under the same no-second-admission rule |
| AI Systems | Bachelor’s; School of AI, College of AI | Same undeclared entry; systems-oriented AI route | Same |

| Electrical Engineering | Bachelor’s; School of Electrical Engineering | Same general KAIST admission; useful for computer engineering, hardware, embedded systems and AI systems. | Same undeclared-major rule. |

**Best programme for me:** Computer Science is the broadest fit for software, algorithms and data work. AI Computing or AI Systems is the more focused choice if the final curriculum and career goal are clearly AI-centered. Electrical Engineering is rational when the portfolio includes robotics, hardware, signal processing or embedded computing.

## C. Application rounds and deadlines

## F. NIS route

- KAIST does not publish a named NIS qualification route or required NIS Higher Level grades.
- NIS is therefore reviewed as the applicant’s official high-school curriculum, not automatically as the ordinary Kazakhstan Attestat route.
- Upload school transcripts, an expected-graduation letter, the NIS school profile and an explanation of the grading scale. Add the NIS Grade 12 certificate after release.
- KAIST expressly permits predicted results for IB/A-level; it does **not** expressly confirm NIS predicted grades as a standardized-test substitute.
- A national school-leaving/entrance result may satisfy the standardized-test category only if accompanied by the required one-page explanation of the exam system, process, competitiveness and result. Ask whether the NIS final qualification is accepted in that category.
- June 2027 final results should fall before the 31 August graduation eligibility date, but the exact post-offer apostille deadline is released with the decision and remains **TBA**.
- NIS English-medium schooling is not an automatic waiver. A waiver may be considered if the entire high-school curriculum was taught in English and the school issues the required official letter.

## G. Academic and testing requirements

### Official minimum

- Graduate (or be expected to graduate) by **31 August 2027** and meet the published international-citizenship rules.
- Submit at least one recognized standardized academic test category.
- Submit English proficiency or qualifying official exemption evidence.
- No GPA, NIS grade, SAT total or Math minimum is published.

### Competitive target — analysis, not a KAIST statistic

The university emphasizes strong mathematics/science achievement. A 1500-class SAT with very strong Math, or excellent externally benchmarked NIS/national/olympiad evidence, would make the academic case clearer; KAIST does not publish a competitive range. With SAT 1300–1350, the application remains possible but KAIST is an extreme reach and portfolio depth cannot erase weak quantitative evidence.

| AP | Accepted | No score minimum; official College Board delivery, code **4433** |

| TOEIC / TEPS | Accepted | TOEIC 720 / TEPS 326 recommended |
| Duolingo / TOEFL ITP / at-home or online tests | Not accepted | — |

English score earliest validity dates in the guide: **12 Nov 2024** for Early and **4 Feb 2025** for Regular. Late delivery is risky; official SAT/AP/ACT delivery should be ordered 1–2 weeks early.

## H. Internal exam and interview

No routine internal Math/Physics/programming exam is published. KAIST may invite selected applicants to an **online interview** on the stated track date. It is not required for every applicant, and the public guide does not publish its length, subjects or numerical weight.
